transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Once I start eating, especially at night after work, I feel like I can’t stop or control how much I’m eating. It’s like a switch flips and I just lose all control, and I've finally reached a point where I know I need help to deal with it.
After these episodes, do you try to undo the eating in any way, like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot? Or do the episodes happen without those behaviors?

I don't make myself throw up or use laxatives, but I definitely try to make up for it. The next day, I'll punish myself by only drinking coffee and forcing myself to walk laps around the fairgrounds or mall parking lot for hours until my knees ache. I feel like I have to burn it all off before I deserve to eat real food again.
How often do these out-of-control eating episodes happen, and for about how many months has this been going on?
This has been happening at least once or twice a week for about four months now. It started getting really bad around the time my new sales initiative at work ramped up.
How much do your weight or body shape affect how you feel about yourself? Are you very afraid of gaining weight?

It affects me completely—lately, whenever I walk into the office or a client dinner, all I can think is, "Do they see how big I’ve gotten in this suit?" If the scale is up even a single pound in the morning, I feel like a complete failure as a person and at my job, no matter how good my sales numbers actually look.

The patient reports recurrent episodes of loss-of-control overeating occurring 1–2 times weekly for about 4 months, followed by compensatory behaviors through fasting/restriction the next day and prolonged excessive exercise. Self-evaluation is markedly overinfluenced by weight/shape and there is strong fear of weight gain. These features support keeping F50.2 as the leading candidate. Other nearby possibilities are less likely because the presence of regular compensatory behaviors argues against a diagnosis defined by binge episodes without such behaviors.

opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Recurrent binge-eating episodes with loss of control are present 1–2 times weekly for 4 months, accompanied by recurrent compensatory behaviors (fasting/restricting intake the next day and prolonged excessive exercise). Self-evaluation is markedly overinfluenced by weight/shape and fear of weight gain. This pattern is most consistent with bulimia nervosa rather than binge-eating disorder because compensatory behaviors are clearly present.
